name: Gedser grid-connected wind plant
description: An experimental wind plant supplied electricity to a Danish alternating-current network.

impact.note: One experimental plant, but its three-blade stall-regulated layout became the pattern for the Danish wind industry and modern turbines.

places.note: Place refers to the sourced event; historic political boundaries are not inferred.

date.basis: Date stated in the cited source.

events.statement: The Gedser experimental wind plant was completed in summer 1957.

evidence.locator: UN proceedings W/17, summary and Gedser mill
evidence.supports: Juul reports a 200 kW plant completed in 1957, put into service in June 1958, with Danish government grants for the pilot and three measuring stations; the plant cost 272,000 Danish crowns excluding other specified costs.
Museum credits Johannes Juul with the design of the Gedser wind turbine.

events.caveats: Completion is distinct from its later entry into service. The museum describes operation in 1957; Juul says formal service began June 1958 after adjustments and measurements.

evidence.supports: Museum credits Johannes Juul with the design of the Gedser wind turbine.

links.statement: Juul says Gedser was designed substantially from experience with the earlier Vester Egesborg and Bogø experimental plants.
links.scope: Source-described development relationship between these records.
links.alternatives: Other antecedents may also have contributed.
links.caveats: A historical design relation, not a claim that the earlier apparatus was a component of the later one.
links.timing: The described earlier event predates the later event.

evidence.supports: Juul describes the 1950 Vester Egesborg plant, 1952 Bogø conversion, and their contribution to Gedser design.
